newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Air Philippines to buy 15 planes from UAL.
newsitem.headline: Air Philippines to buy 15 planes from UAL.

text.p: Air Philippines said on Sunday it has agreed to buy 15 Boeing 737 jets from United Airlines over the next two years for $90 million as part of a massive expansion plan.
It has also been allowed to resume operations following a suspension at the end of last month.

Air Philippines "just concluded a five aircraft purchase agreement with United Airlines with all the planes to be delivered within the year", Air Philippines president Peter Salud said in a statement on Sunday.
"The first delivery is expected some time next week."
Ten more 737s will be bought from United and added to Air Philippines' fleet next year, the statement said.
Air Philippines spokesman Peter Sing said the total cost of the purchases would be around US$90 million.

The company's announcement of its ambitious growth plans follows a decision on Saturday by the Philippine Air Transportation Office (ATO) to lift an order suspending the operations of the domestic carrier.
The ATO temporarily suspended the airline's operations on August 30 after discovering broken parts in two of the airline's three Boeing 737s during a routine inspection.
The airline also has four Japanese-made YS-11 turbo prop aircraft.
Salud welcomed the lifting of the suspension order. He commended the ATO for "its dedication to ensure safety in air transport in the country".
The airline was formed by a group of Filipino businessmen and is based in the Subic free port near Manila.
